runs.text: The visible building features follow the Cadw survey photograph of 29 July 1988 (GHF-E106-R37-A2, disclosed under ATISN 27021): the two-storey rendered stone farmhouse with weathered whitewash, slate roof, three chimney stacks (two stone, one red brick), gabled timber porch, dry-stone garden wall with garden plants, the lower pantile-roofed side wing, outbuildings to the west and faint overhead power lines. Surface textures, vegetation and any detail hidden in the photograph are derived finishes, not record.

The Heneb Historic Environment Record GGAT02038s (R. F. Suggett, December 1988; RCAHM Inventory IV.2 p.582 no.445) records farmhouse and barn “built of local lias limestone, and occupied an historic site next to the parish church … Externally both farmhouse and barn appeared to be of C19th date. Internally, however, surviving vernacular detail – a blocked stone fireplace stair and ogee-stopped beams – suggested a C17th date for the house.” The same record classifies Great House as a sub-medieval house of direct-entry type – cross-passage end-chimney plan with masonry partitions and external wall batter on the unreconstructed north side – its core possibly medieval.

) states: “The seventeenth century phase is associated with the Vaughan Family, the nineteenth century work with the Bute Estate.” Setting from the OS six-inch map Glamorgan XLVII.NW revised 1947 (GHF-E106-R61-A1): the house and yard between the wooded old limekiln and quarry ground to the north and open ground to the south-east, beside St Dochdwy's church.

Working interpretation, openly qualified. This image re-renders the documented 1988 appearance only; no feature is dated earlier than the photograph and the official-record descriptions quoted. The construction dates of the porch, the three chimney stacks, the windows and the pantile side wing are not established by the held sources - the HER dates the exterior only to a C19th character, and the C17th and possible medieval phasing rests on interior detail and plan form that this exterior view does not show.

The rear elevation, interior and roof trusses are unrecorded in the held sources (the 1974 survey covered the ground floor only; access was limited by the ownership dispute). Minor rendering deviations from the photograph are possible in a generated image; the photograph remains the record and this image must never be cited as a source alongside it. The image does not support or weaken any title, phase or family-history position. Both assets are 2D images; the wireframe twin is a 2D architectural line illustration, not a 3D model.

excluded.text: The C17th and possible medieval phases - that evidence is interior detail and plan form, which this exterior view does not depict.
Construction dates of the porch, chimney stacks, windows and pantile side wing - not established by the held sources.
Rear elevation, interior and roof trusses - unrecorded in the held sources (the 1974 survey covered the ground floor only).
People, animals, vehicles and any event other than the 1988 record itself.
The barn across the yard - catalogued separately as AR-REC-0002.

runs.text: The visible building features follow the Cadw survey photograph of 29 July 1988 (GHF-E106-R37-A3, disclosed under ATISN 27021): the single-storey rubble lias-limestone barn with slate roof and red clay ridge tiles; the small gabled projection at the west end with an open arched doorway partly covered by climbing vegetation; the tall central shuttered opening; the louvred slit vents in the east gable; the two low arched openings at the base of the east wall; dressed-stone quoins; the overgrown foreground and hedge. Surface textures, vegetation and any detail hidden in the photograph are derived finishes, not record.

The Heneb Historic Environment Record GGAT02038s (R. F. Suggett, December 1988) records: “Great House Farmhouse and barn formed an attractive group, built of local lias limestone, and occupied an historic site next to the parish church” and “Externally both farmhouse and barn appeared to be of C19th date.” The barn was demolished with the farm buildings on 6 December 1988 (the same HER; GGAT assessment

Working interpretation, openly qualified. The barn's build date is not established: the HER records only that its exterior appeared C19th in character, and no held source dates the barn's fabric, so no earlier date is depicted or implied. The slit vents, arched openings and quoins are drawn only as recorded in 1988.

The interior, roof structure and the barn's working history are unrecorded in the held sources. This image re-renders the documented 1988 appearance only; the photograph remains the record and this image must never be cited as a source alongside it. The image does not support or weaken any title, phase or family-history position. Both assets are 2D images; the wireframe twin is a 2D architectural line illustration, not a 3D model.

excluded.text: The barn's build date - no held source dates its fabric; the HER records a C19th exterior character only.
Interior, roof structure and working history - unrecorded in the held sources.
People, animals, vehicles and any event other than the 1988 record itself.
The farmhouse across the yard - catalogued separately as AR-REC-0001.
